clue.text: Show no concern in row about a pig

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a row is placed around the pig

parts.note: a din is a noisy row or racket
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to care about an argument over a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the noise around the pig, splitting the row after its second letter; 'Show no concern in' is a verb phrase meaning to repudiate.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject or repudiate something is to refuse any further interest or responsibility for it.

clue.text: Seems the exhausted rugger player can go no further

parts.note: dead can mean utterly tired, as in dead on one's feet
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby union

explanation.surface: A worn-out rugby forward can't run another step.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugger is British slang for rugby union; the lock is a forward in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a situation in which neither side can make further progress.

clue.text: Rates apt to be put on one side

indicators.note: the letters are to be put into a new order, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: Tax rates suitable to be shelved for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put' signals rearranging RATES and APT. Rates are a British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated or separated from the rest is placed off to the side.

clue.text: Turpin's last word to Black Bess?

definitions.text: Turpin's last word to Black Bess?

parts.words: Turpin's last word to Black Bess?
parts.note: the highwayman Dick Turpin's famous horse was Black Bess; the last thing a rider says is the call to make a horse stop

explanation.surface: The highwayman's final words to his mare.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman, legendary for riding his mare Black Bess; 'last word' means the command to halt, not a dying utterance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the traditional command to bring a horse to a standstill.

clue.text: Honorary title of key value to America

parts.note: E is a musical key
merit means worth or value
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A ceremonial title that is worth a great deal to the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired professor keeps this honorific added to the former rank, as a mark of distinction.

clue.text: Quite a lot -and then some

parts.note: describes an amount beyond even a large one, greater than at any earlier time

explanation.surface: A great deal, and still more on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in greater measure than at any time before, i.e. a large amount and extra.

clue.text: Toppriority plant

definitions.meaning: a job marked with this word must be done urgently, as top priority
a marsh plant with tall hollow stems

explanation.definitionFit: Urgent work gets this label stamped on it, and the same word names a grasslike waterside plant used for weaving seats.

clue.text: Domestic storm centre

parts.note: a domestic is a household row, and the idiom 'a storm in a ...' places such a fuss in a small piece of crockery

explanation.surface: The heart of a household squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a storm in a teacup' means a big fuss over a trivial matter; 'Domestic' plays on a household quarrel and household china.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a trivial fuss places the storm inside this little drinking vessel.

clue.text: Part of the sailing vessel put to bed

definitions.meaning: on a yacht the ropes controlling the sails have this name
linen laid on a bed when making it up

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the lines trimming sails by this name, and the same word means bed linen, which is laid on a bed.

clue.text: Painting for little Arthur's benefit?

parts.note: painting is a form of art
taken as written
Art is a short form of the name Arthur, with the possessive kept
for someone's sake means for their benefit

explanation.surface: A picture painted to please young Arthur.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints ACTFOR for the first light, but the wordplay and the well-known slogan both give ART FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine holds that painting and other creative work need serve only its own aesthetic purpose.

clue.text: See 9
Using standard method to halt the race

definitions.text: Using standard method to halt the race

parts.words: Using standard method to halt the race
parts.note: a standard is a flag, and waving one is how officials stop a motor race; tiring also suggests a runner losing pace

explanation.surface: Stopping a race in the usual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like 'usual', but it means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Signalling a vehicle or race to stop by waving a banner is the phrase's sense.

clue.text: Soft seats for cats' consumption

definitions.meaning: the tops of seated people's thighs, where a pet might settle
cats drink by taking liquid up with the tongue

explanation.definitionFit: A seated person's thighs make a soft resting place, and the same word means a cat's tongue-drinking of milk.

clue.text: Deadly sin of a tropical tree-dweller

definitions.meaning: one of the seven deadly sins, idleness
a slow-moving South American mammal that hangs in trees

explanation.definitionFit: Laziness is one of the seven deadly sins, and the same word names the slow animal living in rainforest canopies.

clue.text: Wager a modest sum at the Curragh

definitions.text: a modest sum at the Curragh
definitions.meaning: the Curragh is an Irish racecourse, and the former Irish pound had this name

explanation.definitionFit: To gamble small stakes is to make a bet, and the old Irish currency unit, a pound, carried the same name.

clue.text: Carriage to return with the meat

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: return means the little word to goes back, reading in reverse

explanation.surface: A coach driver goes back with the joint for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a leg of lamb or mutton, a cut of butcher's flesh.

clue.text: Charles hungry in the mess

indicators.note: in places the empty letter within the short form of the name

parts.note: hungry suggests an empty stomach, so nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: Charles feels peckish in the officers' dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is a military dining hall, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter disorder or confusion is a muddle or shambles.

clue.text: One use for the ticker-tape machine?

definitions.text: One use for the ticker-tape machine?

parts.words: One use for the ticker-tape machine?
parts.note: the ticker is slang for the heart, and a machine recording its beats on a paper strip

explanation.surface: A purpose for the old stock-price printing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticker-tape' suggests stock-market tickers, but the ticker is the heart and the tape its printed trace.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording heart activity as a trace on paper is a medical diagnostic technique.

clue.text: One well-intentioned the Artful Dodger makes rings round

indicators.note: round means the rearranged name goes around the two rings
artful suggests crafty rearrangement of the name that follows

parts.note: taken as written
two rings look like the letters O O

explanation.surface: Dickens's pickpocket runs rings round a kindly person.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; 'Artful' shuffles the name and 'round' sets the rings in its middle, while 'makes' and 'the' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: A benevolent but often naive person who meddles in trying to help others.

clue.text: Perverse as insurgent Jack in depression

indicators.note: in places the rebel inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A rebel down in a slump behaves wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade was an English rebel leader of 1450, so 'insurgent Jack' is one piece; 'in' sets him inside the hollow, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally degenerate and self-indulgent behaviour can be described as perverse.

clue.text: Situation where expedition is required for victory

definitions.text: Situation where expedition is required for victory

parts.words: Situation where expedition is required for victory
parts.note: expedition here means speed rather than a journey, and the phrase urges haste before defeat

explanation.surface: A military expedition is needed to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' suggests a journey, but here it means promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges immediate haste because delay will mean failure.

clue.text: She appears with George, neve-list and artist

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of a French woman novelist
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman is seen with a man called George, a writer and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like a man's name but leads to the novelist George Sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Musketeer-one in sheep's ole-thing

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Musketeer-one in sheep's ole-thing' ('clothing'): A RAM IS needs 'one' for both A and I, or reads as a cryptic phrase with no full mechanism

clue.text: Sound of music current in Yorkshire

indicators.note: the clue asks for something that sounds like the musical word when spoken

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Melody heard flowing through a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, a county in northern England; 'current' means a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshire river is a flowing body of water, i.e. a current.

clue.text: Looked askance

parts.note: askance means sideways, and the older sense of the verb is to glance sideways, often amorously

explanation.definitionFit: Its original meaning is to cast sidelong glances, which is what looking askance literally describes.

clue.text: Turn of a German star

indicators.note: turn tells us to flip the following letters back to front

parts.note: von is the particle in many German names, as in von Braun

explanation.surface: A German film star gets a twist in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses the joined letters A and VON.
explanation.definitionFit: A suddenly brightening star, flaring up to many times its normal brilliance.

clue.text: Tarry with a nautical guy

definitions.meaning: a guy is a rope, and on a ship a supporting rope for a mast

explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to linger, and on board ship a rope bracing a mast carries the same name.

clue.text: Time in America to capitulate

definitions.meaning: to surrender, as a city does

explanation.definitionFit: Americans call autumn by this word, and a besieged town that surrenders is said to do this.

clue.text: Feeling after Division I loss of place

indicators.note: after places the feeling behind the single letter
I is the Roman numeral one, so the first letter of the word Division

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling

explanation.surface: A team's mood after a first-division relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: Division I reads as a football league; I as one picks the first letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moved to a lower rank or position means losing one's standing.

clue.text: Worker with the French title

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A labourer with an aristocratic French rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A name or title used to refer to someone is informally called this.

clue.text: Testing for quality as a saw

parts.note: a saw is an old proverb, a saying

explanation.surface: Checking that a carpentry tool is up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a tool, but it means a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysing metal to establish its purity is checking its quality.

clue.text: Fighting drink on tap

parts.note: in boxing slang blood is called after a red wine, and to tap it is to make a nose bleed

explanation.surface: A drink served from the barrel at a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boxing slang calls blood by the name of the red Bordeaux wine; 'tapping' it means drawing blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Bordeaux wine is a drink, and the same word is old boxing slang for blood.
